Pentaho Metadata Editor: The graphical modelling tool (PME) used to build a business-friendly semantic layer over physical databases. It maps tables and columns to business terms, defines relationships and calculations, and publishes metadata domains for ad-hoc reporting — all without writing SQL.
Metadata domain: The complete model PME produces and publishes (as an XMI file). It bundles the physical layer, one or more business models, and the business views, giving reporting tools a single business-oriented data source.
Semantic layer: A business-oriented abstraction over raw database structures. It lets non-technical users build reports with familiar terms (Customer Name, Order Total) instead of technical table/column names and SQL.
Physical layer: The technical side of a domain: database connections, physical tables, and physical columns that mirror the actual database. Not every connection here is used by every business model.
Connection: A JDBC database connection defined in the physical layer (e.g. hsqldb:sampledata). A business model references exactly one connection — you cannot mix tables from two connections in one model.
Physical table: An imported reference to a real database table in the physical layer, holding the columns and any base metadata you enrich on them. Prefixed PT_ in PME.
Physical column: An imported reference to a database column in the physical layer. Prefixed PC_. You can also create calculated physical columns from an expression, e.g. [QUANTITYORDERED]*[PRICEEACH].
Business model: The container that turns physical tables into a business-oriented model for a specific analytical purpose. It references one connection and holds business tables, business columns, and relationships. Each gets a system ID such as BV_MODEL_1.
Business table: A business-layer table that references a physical table (e.g. BT_PRODUCTS_PRODUCTS → PT_PRODUCTS). It inherits the physical table's metadata, which you can override per property. Multiple business tables can reference one physical table.
Business column: A business-layer column referencing a physical column, with a friendly name and metadata. It inherits the physical column's properties until overridden.
Metadata inheritance: PME's mechanism where business objects inherit metadata from the physical objects they reference (and from parent concepts), property by property, unless and until the business object overrides a given property.
Relationship: A join PME defines between business tables (one-to-many, many-to-one, etc.) so it can automatically generate correct SQL joins when users build reports. Visible in the model's graphical view.
Star schema: A modelling pattern with a central fact table joined to dimension tables. The OrdersME / OrderStarCustomer business models join ORDERFACT to PRODUCTS, CUSTOMER_W_TER, and DIM_TIME with N:1 relationships.
Business view: The user-facing presentation layer of a business model. It exposes a curated set of business columns organised into categories with business-friendly names for report builders.
Category: A logical grouping of business columns inside a business view (e.g. Orders, Customers, Products). Categories mirror how the business thinks about data, hiding the underlying table structure.
Concept: A reusable bundle of metadata properties (formatting mask, alignment, aggregation, hidden flag) defined once in the Concept Editor and applied to many columns so formatting stays consistent across the domain.
Concept Editor: The PME tool (Tools > Concept Editor) for defining and arranging the concept hierarchy — adding properties to concepts and building parent/child relationships such as Base → Number → USCurrency.
Parent concept: The concept a business object inherits from. Assigned with Set Parent Concept; the object then inherits that concept's properties (e.g. setting USCurrency on a Price column applies $#,##0.00 formatting).
Mask for Number or Date: A concept/column property that formats numeric or date values, e.g. #,##0 (Number), $#,##0.00;($#,##0.00) (Currency), or MM-dd-yyyy (Date). Applies only to numeric/date data types.
Hidden concept: A concept (child of ID) that sets 'Hidden For the User?' so a technical field — like an internal Employee Number — is excluded from report interfaces while still formatted correctly when accessed.
Aggregation: The default rollup applied to a measure column (Sum, Average, Minimum, Maximum). Set on the business/physical column so reports total figures correctly.
Calculated column: A business or physical column derived from an expression over other columns (columns referenced as [COLUMN]), e.g. Total = [QUANTITYORDERED]*[PRICEEACH] or a concatenated Contact Name.
XMI: XML Metadata Interchange — the file format a metadata domain is published/exported as. The published XMI on the Pentaho Server is what reporting tools consume as a data source.
Publish to Server: The PME action (File > Publish To Server) that deploys a domain to the Pentaho BA Server via the metadata import endpoint, making it available as a data source for Interactive Reporting.
MQL: Metadata Query Language — the query model PME and the reporting tools use against a metadata domain. PME generates SQL from MQL using the model's relationships, columns, and constraints.
Query Builder: The PME tool for assembling and previewing a query against a business model — selecting business columns, applying constraints/ordering — to validate the model before publishing.
Interactive Report: A web-based, drag-and-drop ad-hoc report built in the Pentaho User Console against a published metadata domain. Used throughout the course to validate that a domain and its concepts work for end users.
Metadata security: Authorization applied in the metadata model controlling which roles can access the domain and its tables/columns. Enforced once at the model layer so every report inherits it.
Row-level security: A data constraint that filters the rows a user sees based on their role — for example, a Power User / SUZY only seeing Customers where Territory = 'EMEA' while Admin sees all rows.
Data constraint: A model-level filter (often role-based MQL) that restricts which rows are returned for a given user or role, implementing row-level security on a business table.
Pentaho Server: The BA Server that hosts published metadata domains and runs the Pentaho User Console, where learners log in to publish domains, refresh caches, and build Interactive Reports.
Pentaho User Console: The browser-based home of the Pentaho Server (PUC, http://localhost:8080), where you manage data sources, refresh the metadata cache, and create Interactive Reports on a published domain.
SteelWheels: The fictional model-car company whose sample database (SampleData) backs the course. Its 13 interconnected tables (customers, products, orders, employees, financials) are modelled throughout.
SampleData: The HSQLDB sample database (connection hsqldb:sampledata) the workshops model — ORDERFACT, PRODUCTS, CUSTOMER_W_TER, DIM_TIME, ORDERDETAILS, and related tables.
ORDERFACT: The central fact table in the Steel Wheels data, holding transactional sales rows joined to the Customers, Products, and Time dimensions to form the star schema.
DIM_TIME: The time dimension table joined to ORDERFACT via TIME_ID, enabling date-based analysis (year/quarter/month) in the business model.
Refresh metadata cache: Clearing the server's cached metadata after publishing so the User Console picks up the new or changed domain — the metadata equivalent of refreshing the Mondrian schema cache.
Domain repository: The central store on the Pentaho Server where published metadata domains live, making them discoverable and reusable by reporting tools subject to security.
